correctness.rationale: For every nonempty white mask W, exposure counts outside unique-neighbor vertices exactly. The established fort equivalence proves two-leak success iff the complement of a blue set contains no exposure<=2 subset. The subset recurrence is proved by induction and evaluated on all 2^N masks, N<=20, with no unvisited cases. The enumerator checks all coefficient counts and minimal-fort certificates. A separate direct forcing simulator validates every set with 0-2 leaks for all four graph inputs N<=12, and all 2360 optimal sets plus deterministic samples in N=20; it ran 594303 individual leak tests on the dodecahedron. An explicit isomorphism certificate checks its GP(10,2) identity and the other graph inputs. Full infinite assertions are not made. Source and input integers fit the chosen bit widths.

originality.rationale: Prior work already supplies the fort obstruction test, general exact enumeration and some small-graph minimum forcing numbers. The assessed new finite statements are the fully evaluated two-leak cardinality polynomials for all five Platonic skeletons and especially the exact dodecahedral and icosahedral minimal-fort distributions. The 2025 primary generalized-Petersen paper explicitly stops its exact two-leak table at GP(9,2), while its general two-leak upper bound is restricted to k>=7 and does not imply the GP(10,2) counts. The 2026 general polynomial paper offers an algorithm that in principle can derive these exact numbers, but does not evaluate or print these particular coefficients or fort spectra. No same-claim source identified in targeted searches; residual priority uncertainty is recorded.

value.rationale: Exact complete finite classification on the five canonical Platonic skeletons is a natural fault-tolerant propagation benchmark, not an arbitrary graph slice. The exact two-leak forcing polynomials record the number and size distribution of resilient placements. Most significantly, the previously known dodecahedral one-leak optimum 6 jumps to 9 under two leaks, with exactly 2360 optimal choices, and its 1205 inclusion-minimal 2-leak forts exhibit a five-size spectrum. The icosahedron has 240 optimal eight-vertex choices and 255 inclusion-minimal forts all of size four. These complete precise enumerators and obstructions are not inferable numerically from the previously published scalar minima alone, and can serve as benchmarks for future enumeration and structure conjectures; a general-family theorem is not claimed.
